contrast_warning_example.text: Dynamic shading barely changes through the day here: at noon the corals get 30 % of open-water light, in the morning and afternoon 36 %. Only 0.8 % of the light at 10 m arrives as the sun beam; the rest is scattered light from all directions, which the canopy blocks at every hour. A stronger midday contrast needs less scattering water (lower w0), a shallower site or a wider canopy, which also gives less light overall.
